subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: The Normalization of Watching
description: One-minute skill: The Normalization of Watching.

hook.text: Ring doorbells watch the street. Nest cameras watch the house. We surveil ourselves voluntarily.

buildup.text: Consumer surveillance products are marketed as safety tools. Over 10 million Ring cameras are installed.

discovery.text: Amazon shares Ring footage with police — sometimes without the homeowner's knowledge or consent.

twist.text: We resist government cameras but buy corporate ones. The difference is only who profits.

climax.text: When surveillance becomes a consumer product, resistance feels pointless. It's just how life works now.

punchline.text: We fought big brother. Then we bought one.

quiz.question: How has consumer technology normalized surveillance?
options: People voluntarily install cameras that share data with police
Governments force citizens to buy cameras
Consumer cameras don't actually record anything
